purpose: One human-operated supported ChatGPT browser sign-in needed to prepare a separate scientific reviewer; no model invocation.
authorized_native_effects: Human completes the installed Codex client's normal ChatGPT browser login under existing account and workspace policies.

Native client may create its private credential cache ~/.codex/auth.json and ordinary private login/log/cache/support files within existing ~/.codex or the project. Configured log directories elsewhere must cause refusal.

Native client may perform its built-in prior-authentication cleanup/revocation. Wrapper requires the observed file credential backend and an absent auth.json immediately before starting; it does not knowingly replace an existing login.

Native client may open a Windows browser or print a private login URL, bind its local callback, and contact the configured OpenAI authentication service. Browser cookies/session changes are part of this human-operated sign-in.

Native browser authentication may obtain an optional API-key-style token and store it with ChatGPT auth mode. This permission covers native token management only; it authorizes no API model use or charges.
Project wrapper may create only its nonsecret fixed attempt/report receipt under the project delivery directory.
forbidden_actions: No assistant access to credential values; no credential copying, export, hashing, upload or publication.
No raw native terminal/browser output or native logs included in the report.
No API-key login, API model call, paid credits, purchases, credit resets or additional spending.
No change of HOME, CODEX_HOME, authentication backend, account security settings, managed policies or model settings.
No scientific reviewer/model invocation, unattended loop or claim that sign-in establishes entitlement, usage allowance or reviewer independence.
No reading or modifying the other research programme.
If an existing credential file, changed provenance, occupied callback port or incomplete prior attempt is detected, stop and preserve it.
approval_protocol: Publish checkpoint015 first. Human appends ## ANSWER, standalone APPROVE_G0_SIGNIN_015, and scope_sha256: <SHA256 of this exact file> to state/ESCALATION.md, commits and pushes, then pulls that answer before --sign-in. The wrapper requires this recorded authorization.
